issues.issue: Did the officer base the finding that the marriage was not bona fide on erroneous findings of fact made in a perverse or capricious manner?
issues.applicant_position: Officer relied on wrong relationship dates, an erroneous factual finding that undermines the bona fides finding.
issues.respondent_position: The officer was justified in not being convinced of the marriage's bona fides; the onus was on the applicant.
issues.result_quote: On the other hand, it is clear that this finding was not made in a perverse or capricious manner.

issues.issue: Did the officer rely on evidence not put to the applicant, without giving her a chance to respond?
issues.applicant_position: Officer relied on unexplained evidence and did not ask for more; the applicant was ready to provide any evidence on her marriage.
issues.respondent_position: The onus was on the applicant to make her case, not on the officer to ask her to do so.
issues.result_quote: The onus is therefore on the applicant to file any material evidence demonstrating the bona fides of the marriage.

issues.issue: Did the officer err in her analysis of the integration component (hardship and ties to Canada)?
issues.respondent_position: The officer's assessment of the facts on H&C grounds was not unreasonable.
issues.result_quote: Here again, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the Officer’s decision was unreasonable.

issues.issue: Do the officer's findings show a reasonable apprehension of bias?
issues.applicant_position: The officer's findings demonstrate that she was biased against the applicant.
issues.respondent_position: The officer did not demonstrate bias in identifying gaps in the applicant's evidence.
issues.result_quote: Obviously, that is insufficient to demonstrate a reasonable apprehension of bias.
